gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Gugi bends its tall lowercase like a single wire, while Noto Sans Wancho hulks below in heavy, chalky strokes. Lean wire above, pressed chalk beneath: they feel like opposites that agree.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Gugi builds its letters from rods, not carved blades. Noto Sans Warang Citi follows with words that settle into solid blocks, so a page of it reads smoothly, channels opening into every counter.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi has a deep midsection and rounds left unlatched, like an open hook. Noto Sans Yi sits under the steady drafting-pen line of Gugi, a sans-serif with give beside that precision.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-squar: Gugi runs one monoline stroke from start to finish, tall lowercase nearly touching its capitals. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square, a sans-serif with wide gaps and a soaring x-height, keeps small text crisp under that bold voice.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-traditional-nushu: Gugi draws a plain, unmodulated outline, while Noto Traditional Nushu uses a broad-nibbed pen stroke whose bowls fill the line. Machine-cut outline meets hand-pushed pen: that friction is the draw.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-numans: Numans coils its swollen lowercase tight and pushes the tracking well past normal, with each s hanging far from its spine. And Gugi, with no swing in stroke weight, holds the whole thing together.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-onest: Tall lowercase that nearly climbs to the capitals defines Gugi. Onest, a sans-serif with short ascenders over big bowls, keeps a gentle monotone of line thickness, so paragraphs glide along.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-orienta: Orienta lets its counters breathe like a hollow reed cut open, with lowercase hardly shorter than the capitals. Gugi, with curves that carry no stress, stays blunt against that openness.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-oxygen: Uniform strokes, tall letters, zero fuss: that is Gugi. Oxygen, a sans whose curves never close back on themselves, keeps long text flowing smoothly, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-parkinsans: Lanky, loud, and cut open at every terminal. Gugi does its best work grabbing attention, while Parkinsans, a sans-serif with one stroke thickness throughout and wide-mouthed letters, stays crisp when shrunk.
